title.name: Bazaar Basra
title.tagline: One year at the market stall

prologue: Basra, in the year 638. The city is new, built of reed and mud brick where the rivers meet.
Your uncle leaves you his market stall, a storeroom with a little stock, and his ledger.
His note: "Each morning, choose. Open the stall and sell, or take the caravan out to buy."
"Keep enough for Friday's rent. Deal honestly on the road. At the year's end, count what you own and pay zakat."
Four seasons of four weeks. You have no money yet, only your uncle's dates. Sell them first.

morning.wantedNone: Nobody has asked for anything yet.
morning.nextShop: You have goods. Open the shop and sell.
morning.nextSetOut: Your shelves are nearly bare. Set out to buy more.
morning.nextFriday: Friday is near. Keep {n} dirham for the rent.
morning.nextBroke: Not enough for rent yet. Sell what you have.
morning.nextQuest: A quest is due this Friday. Check your quests.

notices.badFish: A customer came back with your bad fish. You paid {n} back.
notices.drought: Families from the drought town now buy from your stall.
notices.corner: The salt scheme paid {n} dirham. People in the bazaar talk about it.
notices.salam: The farmer delivered {n} baskets of dates, as agreed.
notices.loanDispute: Your friend says you borrowed 55, not 40. Nothing was written down.
notices.potter: The potter sent {n} dirham of thanks and new customers.
notices.newMuslim: The trader you travelled with now buys from your stall.
notices.debtorPays: The merchant who owed you paid {n} dirham.
notices.teacher: The teacher sends his students to your stall, with {n} dirham of thanks.
notices.traveller: The traveller you helped came back with a gift of {n} dirham.
notices.brother: You delivered the goods to the traveller's brother. He becomes a regular.
notices.mainDone: The merchants' guild pays you {n} dirham. You finished this season's main quest.

shop.setupHint: Tap a slot to choose a good. Set prices with − and +.
shop.nothing: Nothing to sell. Set out first.

setout.title: Where will you go?
setout.suppliesHint: One a stop. This trip needs {n}.

trip.thirsty: Out of supplies. You traded goods for water at the stop.

home.title: Home in Basra
home.nothing: You came back with nothing to sell.

sandstorm.title: Sandstorm
sandstorm.body: A wall of sand rolls toward the caravan.

out.a: You shelter behind the camels until it passes.
out.bLost: The wind tears loose some of your cargo.
out.bLucky: You make it through with everything.

sandstorm.lesson: "Tie your camel, then trust in Allah." Take care first, then trust.

lameCamel.title: A lame camel
lameCamel.body: One of your camels is limping and groans under its load.

out.a: The camel rests and walks on.
out.b: You leave two loads by the road.
out.c: The overloaded camels slow down. The next stop costs double.

lameCamel.lesson: The Prophet ﷺ rebuked a man whose camel was overworked and hungry. Kindness to animals is part of faith.

bandits.title: Riders on the ridge
bandits.body: Scouts are watching the road. They may be bandits.

out.a: You pay your share and travel slowly, but safely.
out.b: You slip past in the dark.
out.cRobbed: They take part of what you carry.

bandits.lesson: Weigh a risk against its cost. There is safety in numbers.

caravanPot.title: The caravan pot
caravanPot.body: The travellers each put 2 dirham into a pot. Whoever loses goods on this trip is paid back from it.

out.a: Your coins go in with everyone's.

caravanPot.lesson: Sharing a loss together is the idea behind takaful. It is mutual help, not a bet.

bedouinCamp.title: A Bedouin camp
bedouinCamp.body: A family invites you to rest, eat and drink with them.

out.a: They fill your water skins and tell you what lies ahead.

bedouinCamp.lesson: Hospitality to guests is a duty in Islam. Local knowledge is worth more than coins.

dampSalt.title: Cheap salt
dampSalt.body: A seller offers salt sacks very cheaply. The bottoms of the sacks look damp.

out.a: You pick out four good sacks.
out.b: Half the sacks are ruined. {n} are usable.

dampSalt.lesson: A seller must show any defect. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever cheats is not one of us."

badFish.title: Badly salted fish
badFish.body: Two of your fish were cured badly. They will not keep long.
badFish.a: Tell buyers and sell them cheap
badFish.b: Mix them in with the good ones

out.a: A cook buys them at a fair low price.

badFish.lesson: The rule of honest selling applies to you too. Hidden faults come back.

droughtTown.title: A town in drought
droughtTown.body: The wells are low and food is short. People crowd around your caravan.

out.a: They thank you and remember your name.
out.b: They pay, and they will remember this too.

droughtTown.lesson: Taking advantage of people in need is wrong. A good name is worth more than one sale.

cornerSalt.title: A salt scheme
cornerSalt.body: A merchant wants partners to buy up all the salt, then sell it dear.

out.a: You hand him your share.
out.b: He shrugs and finds someone else.

cornerSalt.lesson: Hoarding goods to push prices up (ihtikar) is forbidden. It hurts everyone who needs them.

fakeBidder.title: A helpful stranger
fakeBidder.body: A man offers to pretend to bid for your goods in the market, so real buyers pay more.

out.a: Prices rise in the bazaar for a few days.

fakeBidder.lesson: Fake bidding to raise a price (najash) is forbidden.

nextNet.title: The fisherman's net
nextNet.body: A fisherman offers whatever his next net brings up for 10 dirham.

out.aGood: Lucky: the net brings up {n} fish.
out.b: Three good fish, as you saw them.

nextNet.lesson: Buying something unknown (gharar) is forbidden. Buy what you can see.

salam.title: Paying ahead
salam.body: A farmer needs money now. He offers 8 baskets of dates at harvest in two weeks, for 15 dirham today.

out.a: The amount, quality, price and date are agreed.

salam.lesson: Paying now for later goods (salam) is allowed when everything is fixed in advance.

moneylender.title: The moneylender
moneylender.body: He will lend you 50 dirham today. You pay back 60 in two weeks.

out.a: You owe him 60.

moneylender.lesson: Interest (riba) is forbidden. Allah permits trade and forbids riba (Al-Baqarah 2:275).

friendlyLoan.title: A friend's loan
friendlyLoan.body: An old friend of your uncle offers to lend you 40 dirham, with no interest, for two weeks.

out.a: A witness signs. You owe 40.

friendlyLoan.lesson: A loan without interest (qard hasan) is good. Write debts down, says Al-Baqarah 2:282.

widow.title: The widow's capital
widow.body: A wealthy widow offers you 60 dirham to trade with. She takes half the profit, or bears the loss.

out.a: On Friday you settle with her.
out.b: She thanks you for your honesty.

widow.lesson: This partnership is mudarabah. The Prophet ﷺ traded this way with Khadijah's money.

datesForDates.title: Dates for dates
datesForDates.body: A trader offers two baskets of his poor dates for one of your good ones.
datesForDates.b: Sell yours for coin, then buy his

out.a: You swap directly.
out.b: Same result, done the right way.

datesForDates.lesson: Swapping unequal amounts of the same food is riba. The Prophet ﷺ told Bilal: sell, then buy.

shortMeasure.title: The short measure
shortMeasure.body: A trader is filling a widow's bowl short, and still charging her full price.

out.a: He grumbles and fills it properly.

shortMeasure.lesson: "Woe to those who give less than due" (Al-Mutaffifin 83:1). Give full measure.

bigOrder.title: A big order
bigOrder.body: A cook wants {qty} sacks of salt at {price} each. Bring them any morning within {days} days.

out.a: The order is written down. Have the salt ready.
out.b: You shake on it. Have the salt ready.

bigOrder.lesson: Keep your word, and write contracts down so both sides keep theirs.

hungryFamily.title: A hungry family
hungryFamily.body: At the oasis, a mother and her children have had nothing to eat today.

out.a: The children eat. The mother prays for you.
out.b: She thanks you and buys bread.

hungryFamily.lesson: The poor (fuqara) are the first group zakat is for. Charity does not reduce wealth.

potter.title: The potter
potter.body: He works every day, but his pots don't earn enough to feed his family.

out.a: He smiles. You've helped him and made a friend.

potter.lesson: The needy (masakin) are people who work and still fall short. Zakat is for them too.

zakatCollector.title: The zakat collector
zakatCollector.body: An officer of the bayt al-mal is on his rounds. He offers to explain how zakat on trade is counted.

out.a: Nisab is the minimum. After a full year, pay one fortieth of cash and trade goods.

zakatCollector.lesson: Those who collect zakat (amil) are paid from it. Nisab and a full year (hawl) decide what's due.

newMuslim.title: A new Muslim
newMuslim.body: A trader has just embraced Islam. He's unsure of the road and the people.

out.a: You travel together and talk late into the night.

newMuslim.lesson: Zakat may go to those whose hearts are being brought close (muallaf).

freedom.title: Buying freedom
freedom.body: An enslaved man has agreed with his master to buy his freedom. He is 20 dirham short.

out.a: He goes to his master a free man.

freedom.lesson: Freeing people from slavery (riqab) is one of the eight uses of zakat.

debtor.title: The man in debt
debtor.body: The merchant who owed your uncle 20 dirham can't pay. His shop is failing.

out.a: He promises to pay when he can.
out.c: He sells his tools to pay you.

debtor.lesson: "If the debtor is in hardship, give him time" (Al-Baqarah 2:280). Debtors (gharimin) may receive zakat.

teacher.title: The travelling teacher
teacher.body: A teacher on his way to teach in a new town has lost his camel.
teacher.a: Give him a ride (half a day)

out.a: He teaches you a verse on the way.
out.b: You leave him on the road.

teacher.lesson: Zakat may go to good causes in the way of Allah (fi sabilillah).

traveller.title: A stranded traveller
traveller.body: A traveller far from home has been robbed and has no water left.

out.a: He drinks and blesses you. He asks your name.

traveller.lesson: The stranded traveller (ibn as-sabil) is one of the eight groups zakat is for.

lostPurse.title: A lost purse
lostPurse.body: A purse lies in the sand, heavy with coins.
lostPurse.a: Announce it and find the owner

out.a: The owner is found and thanks you.
out.aReward: The owner thanks you and gives you 5 dirham.

lostPurse.lesson: Found property (luqatah) must be announced so the owner can claim it.

carryForBrother.title: Carry this for my brother
carryForBrother.body: A traveller asks you to carry two bundles to his brother in Basra. They take space.

out.a: You load his bundles with care.

carryForBrother.lesson: Goods left in your care (wadiah) are a trust. Deliver them whole.

rumour.title: A rumour
rumour.body: At the caravanserai, men say {good} prices in Basra will jump next week.

out.a: You'll find out in the bazaar.
out.bTrue: It's true. {good} will sell high next week.
out.bFalse: It's false. Someone made it up.

rumour.lesson: "If a sinner brings you news, verify it" (Al-Hujurat 49:6). Check before you act.

buriedCoins.title: Buried coins
buriedCoins.body: In the ruins you find an old pot full of coins.
buriedCoins.a: Give one fifth to the bayt al-mal

out.a: {n} dirham found. {fifth} goes to the bayt al-mal now.

buriedCoins.lesson: Buried treasure (rikaz) owes one fifth at once. Unlike zakat, there is no year to wait.

purser.title: The ship's purser
purser.body: A purser loading a ship for India needs {qty} {good} at {price} each, within {days} days.

out.a: He writes the order down. Bring the goods to the stall.

purser.lesson: "O you who believe, fulfil your contracts" (Al-Ma'idah 5:1).

caravanMaster.title: The caravan master
caravanMaster.body: A caravan leaving for Damascus needs {qty} {good} at {price} each, within {days} days.

out.a: The deal is written and witnessed.

caravanMaster.lesson: You may promise goods you don't have yet if the amount, price and date are clear. Then keep your word.

mosqueKitchen.title: The mosque kitchen
mosqueKitchen.body: The imam feeds the poor after Jumu'ah. He asks for {qty} baskets of dates at {price} each, within {days} days.

out.a: He thanks you and writes your name down.

mosqueKitchen.lesson: Feeding the hungry is among the best of deeds. A promise is a trust to keep.

friday.title: Friday
friday.sub: The market is closed for Jumu'ah.
friday.wholesale: Sold {n} goods to the wholesaler at half price
friday.orderBackedOut: A buyer backed out of a handshake order
friday.orderShort: You did not have the {good} you promised
friday.upgrades: The carpenter and the caravan master

upgradeText.shelf: One more slot. Two more customers a day. Rent goes up.
upgradeText.camel: Carry 5 more goods on each trip.
upgradeText.guide: See every stop on the map.
upgradeText.boy: Empty slots refill themselves from the storeroom.

friday.mainDone: You finished the main quest. The guild paid you {n} dirham.
friday.mainMissed: The main quest wasn't finished this season. A new one starts now.

broke.title: The stall is lost
broke.body: You couldn't pay Friday's rent, even after selling your stock. The landlord gives the stall to another trader.
broke.lesson: Keep enough cash for what you owe. Goods in the storeroom don't pay the rent.

notebook.title: Notebook
notebook.hint: What customers did at each price.
notebook.zakat: Zakat: nisab is 200 dirham. After a full year, pay one fortieth of cash, stock and money owed to you.

bayt.title: The bayt al-mal
bayt.clerk: The clerk opens your ledger. "Let us count what you own today."
bayt.valueHint: Pick the price for each stack.
bayt.wrongPaid: Not what you paid. Trade goods are valued at today's market price.
bayt.wrongHoped: Not what you hope to get. Use the price the market pays today.
bayt.noStock: Your storeroom is empty. Nothing to value.
bayt.fixtures: Your shelves, camels and tools ({n} dirham) are not counted. Zakat on trade is on cash and goods for sale.
bayt.rikaz: Paid on buried treasure this year: {n}
bayt.under: You are under the nisab. No zakat is due this year.
bayt.paid: The clerk writes your zakat in his register.
bayt.sadaqahBody: Zakat is paid. Would you like to give extra, by choice?

asnaf.title: Where zakat goes
scenes: Like the hungry family at the oasis: food for those with nothing.
Like the potter who works and still falls short.
The clerk and the collector are paid for their work.
Like the new Muslim you met on the road.
Like the man buying his freedom.
Like the merchant who could not pay his debt.
Like the teacher travelling to teach a new town.
Like the traveller robbed on the road, far from home.
asnaf.others: Other traders' zakat did this work this year.

end.title: Your year
end.line: Zakat on trade goods is still due today. Count yours.
end.shareText: My year at the Basra bazaar: {profit} dirham profit, amanah {amanah}, {zakat} dirham zakat paid.

quests.title: Quests
mainBody: Show the bazaar your uncle's stall is in good hands.
Grow your trade and help people on the road.
Sell more, build up the stall, keep helping.
A full year of honest trade. Finish strong, then count your zakat.
quests.none: No side quests yet. People on the road may ask you for goods.

repay.friend: Repay {n} dirham to your uncle's friend

quests.backedOut: The buyer backed out. Nothing was written down.
quests.repaid: Debt repaid early. Your name is good in the bazaar.
quests.rule: Each side quest gives at least a week. Finish it early any morning, or it is settled on its Friday.

tutorial.slot: Your uncle left 10 baskets of dates. Tap your slot and put the dates on it.
tutorial.price: Set your price with − and +. Dates are worth about {n} today.
tutorial.open: Open the shop and watch your customers.
tutorial.tooHigh: That is too dear for a first day. Try a lower price.
tutorial.watch: Each customer shows how they feel about your price:
tutorial.restock: The slot is empty. Tap Restock to bring more dates from the storeroom.
tutorial.night: Sold out! That money is your capital. The notebook keeps every price you tried, with the face it got.
tutorial.morning: Each morning, choose: open the shop, or set out to buy more. Your storeroom is empty, so set out to the date groves.
